questions.prompt: What happens when a caller deletes a Derived object through a Base* pointer whose ~Base() destructor is NOT virtual?
options: Only ~Base() runs and Derived::data leaks, which is otherwise well-defined
Both ~Derived() and ~Base() run because operator delete checks heap metadata
The behavior is undefined according to [expr.delete]
The compiler rejects delete p unless Base has at least one virtual function
questions.explanation: Under [expr.delete], deleting a polymorphic or derived-class object through a base pointer whose static type has a non-virtual destructor is undefined behavior—even if Derived adds no non-trivial data members.

questions.prompt: Why does omitting the override specifier on Derived::render below introduce a subtle bug?
options: Button::render lacks const, so it hides Widget::render instead of overriding it
Virtual functions cannot be overridden without repeating the virtual keyword
The compiler automatically converts Widget::render to non-const to match Button
Button becomes an abstract class until override is added
questions.explanation: const-qualification is part of a member function's type. Without override, Button::render(int) declares a brand-new unrelated non-virtual member that hides Widget::render(int) const rather than overriding it.

questions.prompt: What is the result of compiling and calling probe()?
options: Compile error: Derived::value is private
Returns 100 because Derived::value runs with Derived's default argument 99
Returns 10 because virtual calls with private overrides fall back to Base
Compiles and returns 11: access and default arg use Base, dispatch uses Derived
questions.explanation: Access control ([class.access.virt]) and default arguments ([dcl.fct.default]) are checked and substituted statically from Base at the call site b.value(). At runtime, virtual dispatch still invokes Derived::value(10), returning 11.

questions.prompt: What does constructing Derived log when Base's constructor calls the virtual function tag()?
options: "Derived", because the dynamic type of the full object is already Derived
"Base", because inside Base::Base() the object's dynamic type is Base
Undefined behavior whenever any virtual function is called from a constructor
Compile error: virtual functions cannot be called inside constructors
questions.explanation: Under [class.cdtor], while Base::Base() executes, Derived's subobject has not started its lifetime yet, so the dynamic type of *this is Base. Virtual dispatch therefore resolves tag() to Base::tag().

questions.prompt: In virtual diamond inheritance below, what value does Join{}.id hold after construction?
options: 0, because the most-derived class Join initializes Common and omits Common from its initializer list
1, because Left appears first in Join's base-specifier list
2, because Right overwrites Common after Left runs
Ill-formed: Join fails to compile unless it explicitly writes Common(0)
questions.explanation: Under [class.base.init], a virtual base subobject is always initialized by the constructor of the most-derived class (Join). Initializers for Common in Left and Right are ignored, so Join default-initializes Common via Common(0).

questions.prompt: Why does declaring a pure virtual destructor `virtual ~Stream() = 0;` still require providing an out-of-class body `Stream::~Stream() = default;`?
options: Only because linkers always emit vtable slots for destructors even on abstract classes
Because pure virtual functions can never have empty bodies in C++
Because FileStream's destructor implicitly invokes Stream::~Stream() non-virtually during teardown
It is optional unless a caller deletes through Stream*
questions.explanation: Every derived destructor implicitly calls each direct base class's destructor statically (not via virtual dispatch) when tearing down the base subobject ([class.dtor]). Without a definition for Stream::~Stream(), linking FileStream fails.
